deferred_world_transition: GSLevel::LoadLevel calls StateMachine::SwitchState, which only enqueues a switch. The later StateMachine::Update drains it; _switchState pops the old state before pushing the new one. The old GSLevel dtor calls Level::Unload, closes the HUD, deletes the old Level, then clears GSLevel::s_level. Level::Unload itself runs another QuickSave using Level+0xf0, then loading-menu/object-manager cleanup, SG_SaveAllPlayer using that same force byte, sound stop, loaded-state clear, network uninit, PlayerManager update, and RNG reseed. The call order is static source evidence; the current adapter ends at the request boundary.
owner_boundary: The adapter passes one existing Level identity, canonical PlayerSavegame identity, and separate per-level LevelSavegame identity into their existing providers. It does not allocate either Save owner or synchronously destroy/recreate the scene. Selected player and LevelSavegame owners exist, but Level OBJS still depends on exact serializers for live actors; the adapter test does not claim those providers are wired for gameplay.
